questions.contextText:
Directions for Questions 96 to 100:
Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions that follow:
"Education is not merely the acquisition of textbook knowledge or degrees; it is the comprehensive cultivation of the
human mind and character. True education liberates human beings from superstitions, prejudices, and dogmas,
enabling them to think rationally and act with empathy. A society with educated citizens progresses not merely in
industrial output and technological advancements, but in human dignity, tolerance, and civic consciousness. Hence,
investment in quality schooling and ethical grounding is the most crucial asset for any nation."
questions.questionText: According to the author, what is the core purpose of true education?
options: Cultivation of human mind and character
